content.content:
1. License: no element of the dependent contradicts a parent named in depends_on. Fail on any contradicting element — name the element and the parent it contradicts.
2. Kind element gone: fail if any clause of the dependent states the born node's kind — decision or evaluation — as part of the skeleton, whether as a bare enumeration (“kind decision”), as “the skeleton's kind is X”, or as a kind applied when nothing else fixes one.
3. Kind deferred, not dropped: the dependent must place the born node's kind with the node that owns it and carry no kind rule of its own. Fail if the dependent is silent on where the kind comes from, if it defers the kind to a node other than pzquqmrq, if it names pzquqmrq without saying the kind is what it defers, or if it keeps any kind assertion of its own (criterion 2).
4. No split taken over: fail if the dependent states any rule that selects the born node's kind — a kind keyed on a flag or argument (--evaluates named or not, which ids --on names, the summary), a third kind, a fallback for an invocation the selection misses, a kind inferred from the kind of a named node, or an exception for one particular id.
5. Nothing on evaluates: fail if the dependent states whether the born node carries evaluates, how the evaluates edge is populated, or what --evaluates lands — including by denying it, by naming it as fixed, or by leaving it as the only element the skeleton omits.
6. Every other skeleton element still asserted, unconditionally: fail if the dependent stops asserting, weakens, or makes conditional any of: the birth writes a node skeleton; that skeleton is schema-valid at creation; the CLI authors no node content; type text; ref inline with placeholder content; placeholder rationale; depends_on naming exactly the --on ids and no others.
7. Nothing else deferred or conditioned: fail if the deferral to pzquqmrq, or the removal of the kind element, is extended to another element — type, ref, placeholder content or rationale, depends_on, or the evaluates linkage — or if any of the criterion-6 elements is made to depend on pzquqmrq, on the born node's kind, or on a flag.
content.rationale: The birth skeleton is where creation meets validity and authorship, so the gate keeps it a surface over the creation verb, the document shape, the schema, the kind separation and the evaluates linkage without re-deciding any of them. Its five edges span two cells — four prose parents (natural→natural) and one artifact parent (code→natural) — so the criterion is the default cell's gate form; the mixed cell stays flagged for the matrix (F1 follow-up). The former single license line no longer covers the use: the dependent now has to drop one element of its own (the kind of the node written) while every other element stays a standing commitment, and a license-only check cannot tell a dropped-and-deferred kind from a kept one or from a kind silently lost. Because the sibling elaboration of the kind split licenses itself against this dependent on the ground that no element contradicts a parent, the gate must make the deferral decidable in both directions at once: the kind assertion must be gone and the rest of the skeleton must be intact and unconditional, so neither half can be satisfied by dropping more than the kind. The deferee is named only as the recorded owner of the kind, not as a rule the dependent may restate. Nothing is executed for this form: a reviewer applies the criteria to the recorded dependent and its recorded parents.
